findings.title: website_name bypasses TL0 website hiding
findings.body: website is listed in untrusted_attributes, so anonymous viewers of a trust-level 0 user do not receive user_profile.website (anti-spam: the profile must not expose a new user's site). website_name is a new public attribute and is not in that list, and its method reads object.user_profile.website directly. Anonymous clients therefore still get the host, and the path whenever the domain heuristic matches, and user.hbs renders that as the globe label. The new specs never serialize a TL0 user with Guardian.new and assert website_name is absent, so this regression is untested.

findings.title: include_website_name is never invoked
findings.body: ActiveModel::Serializer only calls include_<attr>? (every other hook in this file uses that name). include_website_name has no question mark, so it is dead code and the attribute is always serialized. Users with a blank or unparsable website still get website_name: null in /users/:username.json, and any condition placed in this method will not run.

findings.title: Same-domain path display is case-sensitive
findings.body: website_host is taken from URI#host, which keeps the URL's casing, and is compared to Discourse.current_hostname with == and String#ends_with? (both case-sensitive). A site on example.com and a website of http://Example.com/user, or a site on forums.example.com and a website of http://Example.com/user, fails every branch and the profile shows only the host. The feature then does not show the path for ordinary mixed-case links. The specs only stub lowercase hosts.

findings.title: Domain check mis-classifies hosts and misses www vs apex
findings.body: The equal-label branch treats any two hosts with the same label count above 2 as the same site when every label but the first matches. On a forum at mysite.github.io or forum.co.uk, http://evil.github.io/phish and http://other.co.uk/phish are therefore rendered with the full path, not just the host. The else branch (discourse_host.ends_with?("." + website_host)) is true for any dotted suffix, so a website host of com or co.uk is treated as the parent of a normal forum hostname. The check is also asymmetric for the common www case: instance example.com vs website www.example.com/user does not match (label counts differ, and example.com does not end with .www.example.com), so the path is hidden, while instance www.example.com vs website example.com/user does show the path. None of these cases are covered by the new specs.
